proposal: The Mandate says the SEC and CFTC have handled digital assets mainly through enforcement and recommends a joint regulation under which a holder of a digital asset is not treated as party to an investment contract unless the holder is entitled to a share of enterprise earnings, a defined payment flow, or claims on assets in liquidation; otherwise the asset would be a CFTC-regulated commodity. It also recommends amending the statutory definitions of commodity and security, and, if regulators do not act, that Congress legislate.

status_summary: The agencies have moved in the same general direction through a joint interpretation and a proposed rule, not the joint regulation and statutory definition changes the Mandate specifies. The SEC and CFTC issued a joint interpretation, published and effective 2026-03-23, that sorts crypto assets into five categories, says digital commodities, digital collectibles and digital tools are not securities in themselves (though they can be sold under an investment contract), describes when an investment contract ends, and states that the Howey test remains binding, so it does not adopt the Mandate's test based on entitlement to profits, payment flows or liquidation claims; the CFTC part says some non-security crypto assets could meet the Commodity Exchange Act definition of commodity. The SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets on 2026-08-21, with a $5 million four-year exemption, a $75 million annual exemption and a conditional safe harbor from the investment contract prong, with comments due 2026-10-20. In Congress, the Senate rejected cloture 49-50 on 2026-09-15 on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633, which Crypto Briefing reports passed the House 294-134 in July 2025; the GENIUS Act (P.L. 119-27, 2025-07-18) covers payment stablecoins only.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14178, titled Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology, is signed (published in the Federal Register 2025-01-31).
Crypto Briefing reports that H.R. 3633 passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 (month only is given, so the first of the month is used).
The GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, S. 1582), which provides for regulation of payment stablecoins, is approved.
The SEC and CFTC joint interpretation on the application of the federal securities laws to certain crypto assets is published in the Federal Register and takes effect the same day.
The SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets is published, with a tailored offering regime and a conditional safe harbor from the investment contract prong; comments are due 2026-10-20.
Senate vote 234: cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633 (digital commodity regulation by the SEC and CFTC) is rejected 49-50.

uncertainties: I read summaries of the Federal Register pages (the interpretation and the proposal were truncated at 100,000 characters), not the full releases, so the safe harbor conditions and the wrapping and airdrop sections were not read. The proposal refers to the interpretation by a 2026-03-17 date, while the Federal Register shows publication and effectiveness on 2026-03-23; the 17 March date may be the Commission vote date. The Senate roll call page does not use the CLARITY Act name; the link between H.R. 3633 and that name, and the House 294-134 vote, rest on Crypto Briefing. The Senate roll call list was partly truncated, so a later vote on H.R. 3633 after 2026-09-15 cannot be fully ruled out (none seen through vote 256 on 2026-09-30).
